societies.name: Anthem — The Councils’ protected candle labor
societies.society: Deliberate suppression of demonstrated labor-saving lighting

scope.period: The Councils’ order at Equality’s demonstration, before his escape
scope.population: Humans subject to the city’s assigned occupations and collective homes
exclusions: The escaped couple’s proposed future society
An imagined fully automated economy not demonstrated in the novella

societies.description:
The World Council of Scholars rejects Equality’s demonstrated electric light partly because it would disrupt the candle industry and the plans organizing thousands of workers. A Council member also explicitly condemns relief from toil itself. This is a narrow but direct zero variant: authorities preserve existing work and institutions despite an available labor-saving replacement. The evidence supports lighting and its related labor, not a claim that the city could already automate all production.

Occupations and productive plans are imposed by human Councils, placing control near concentrated human authority. The collective vocabulary does not give workers effective ownership. Food and communal homes exist inside an enforced labor order, while punishment and dependency make their security uncertain; the guarantee estimate is consequently broad and weak. Children, students, assigned workers and elderly residents cannot be converted into a precise nonworking share from the available account. The zero label describes deliberate refusal of a technical opportunity, not literal universal employment or a claim that the society already supplies everyone without work.

guarantees.basis: Collective homes coexist with compulsory assigned occupations and punishment; security of access is weakly established. The primary chapter explicitly rejects labor-saving lighting to preserve candle plans and toil.

control.basis: Human Councils impose occupations and production plans; collective language is not evidence of distributed effective control.

nonworking.basis: No all-age useful-work census; zero variant concerns the rejected labor-saving opportunity, not zero nonworkers.

evidence.claim: Collective homes coexist with compulsory assigned occupations and punishment; security of access is weakly established. The primary chapter explicitly rejects labor-saving lighting to preserve candle plans and toil.
evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

uncertainties: Reference-led provisional assessment; source limitations and editorial uncertainty remain explicit.

societies.name: Landscape with Invisible Hand — Humans under Vuvv production
societies.society: Technological displacement without an ordinary human material floor

scope.continuity: Shared broad book/film Vuvv technological-economy model; specific family plot differences excluded
scope.period: Established Vuvv economic dominance and widespread human displacement
scope.population: Living humans on Earth subject to Vuvv economic control
exclusions: Vuvv residents as humans in the labor denominator
The entire alien civilization’s internal ownership rules
Adaptation-specific family bargains as universal law

societies.description:
Vuvv technology displaces human employment while food, clean water and extraordinary medicine remain unaffordable to ordinary families. The productive breakthrough therefore fails to create a reliable human necessities floor. Selling human cultural performances to alien customers becomes one survival strategy, and widespread displacement is not treated as secure leisure. The same broad arrangement is depicted in the novel and film, without assuming their individual plot events are identical.

Control lies with the biological Vuvv ruling economy. The coordinate near zero is an explicit analogy to concentrated non-machine elite control: alien domination is not autonomous AI sovereignty. The references do not establish how ownership is distributed among the aliens themselves. Human artists, performers, service workers and people seeking income still do useful work. A family’s unemployment, homelessness or desperation cannot yield a population-wide nonworking fraction, so that axis remains unresolved. The exclusion is the reason this fits the weak-guarantee concentrated model, despite the surrounding society’s remarkable technology.

guarantees.basis: The author explicitly links technological job replacement with lack of money for necessities; the film corroborates displacement and homelessness.

control.basis: Biological Vuvv economic domination is disclosed as an analogy to concentrated non-AI control, not evidence of a machine sovereign or a single alien owner.

nonworking.basis: Useful human cultural/service work continues; unemployment and poverty are not a census of everyone doing no useful activity.

evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Dawn — Human residents of the Oankali living ship
societies.society: Engineered biological provision under Oankali authority

scope.period: Awakened human residence aboard the Oankali ship before Earth resettlement
scope.population: Awake living human survivors supported aboard the ship
exclusions: Sleeping humans as nonworking leisure residents
Later Earth resister villages or the Mars-colony agreement
Oankali biology as autonomous AI government

societies.description:
The Oankali ship’s engineered living structures supply food, oxygen, waste processing, transport and living space. Awakened humans receive that support and medical intervention without purchasing it through wages. Designed biological infrastructure functions here as the technological production system. Guarantees are favorable for this limited resident group, while captivity, selection and dependence prevent the stronger claim of a freely chosen universal entitlement.

Final authority belongs to the biological Oankali, whose gene-trade project constrains human futures. Control near zero is explicitly an analogy to a concentrated non-AI provider; the living ship is not automatically classified as a machine sovereign. Reproductive coercion is relevant to the terms of residence, but is not invented as evidence that meals are routinely withdrawn for disobedience. Lilith and other awakened humans learn, train, care and perform useful tasks. Dormant survivors are outside the active population, and the available passages do not supply an all-person work census, leaving nonworking unresolved.

guarantees.basis: Engineered living structures directly provide the necessities of awake human residents without wage purchases; captive and selective residence qualifies coverage.

control.basis: Biological Oankali hold final authority; zero is an explicit non-AI concentrated-provider analogy, not a statement that the living ship is an independent machine government.

nonworking.basis: Training, care and useful learning continue; sleeping survivors are excluded and no active-resident work census is available.

societies.name: Nova Praxis — Coalition citizens’ compiler floor
societies.society: House-associated citizens with a default resource standard

scope.continuity: Official setting, Savage Worlds overview corroborating the Fate-era publisher model
scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived citizen minds
exclusions: Reputation extras as a condition for every basic necessity

societies.description:
Coalition citizens receive a default material standard, with reputation governing resources beyond that baseline. Most own compilers and decompilers that fabricate goods and recycle their inputs. This is direct household-level productive access, not simply a post-scarcity slogan. Guarantees are strong within citizenship, though citizenship itself is a real boundary: Apostates do not share this floor. The overview’s general promotional promise is therefore narrowed to the population the rules actually identify.

Control combines widespread personal machinery and direct political input with House power, surveillance and government enforcement. The coordinate favors distributed human control but keeps a broad interval for those constraints. Mimir’s historical invention does not make Mimir the current ruler, and government monitoring AIs are not assumed sovereign. Active human-derived digital residents are an explicit population proxy. Reputation-producing art, administration, care and technical contributions remain useful work. Receiving a baseline, or owning a compiler, says too little about participation to support a nonworking percentage.

guarantees.basis: Official overview identifies a default resource standard and widespread personal compilers; citizenship exclusions are explicit and reputation governs extras.

control.basis: Personal compiler ownership and political input distribute human authority, qualified by Houses, surveillance and government control; Mimir is shut down and Monitors report to government.

nonworking.basis: Contributions, care and technical work remain useful; active human-derived minds are a disclosed proxy and no all-person participation census is supplied.

evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Nova Praxis — Apostates outside the compiler floor
societies.society: Non-citizen communities excluded from Coalition resource guarantees

scope.period: Established post-Exodus Coalition and surrounding Apostate communities
scope.population: Living human and active human-derived non-citizens
exclusions: Every Apostate community as equally poor

societies.description:
Apostates live outside Coalition citizenship and its resource standard. The official overview describes barter, scavenging and people laboring for Houses in hopes of gaining admission. Molecular production has made ordinary goods cheap inside the supported order, but access is institutionally withheld from this population. The weak guarantee estimate reflects that documented exclusion, while allowing that some independent communities are better organized than others. This materially different access boundary warrants a separate point from supported citizens.

The references do not establish who owns productive equipment across the varied Apostate enclaves, so control remains unresolved. Coalition institutions determine access to their own resources, but that fact is not stretched into ownership of every independent machine. The concentrated-exclusion regime is provisional, with distributed-market alternatives left open. Survival labor, scavenging, trade and work toward citizenship are useful activities. Neither marginality nor lack of formal citizenship is leisure, and no participation percentage is inferred. Active human-derived minds are explicitly included as a proxy; inactive copies are not counted.

guarantees.basis: Official overview explicitly excludes Apostates from Coalition resources and describes survival struggles and labor toward citizenship despite compiler abundance.

control.basis: Enclave ownership differs and is not established; Coalition gatekeeping is not proof that Houses own every independent fabricator.

nonworking.basis: Scavenging, barter, care and labor toward citizenship are useful work; active human-derived minds are an explicit proxy and no census exists.

evidence.locator: Bounded named-society economic and story sections

societies.name: Eclipse Phase — Extropia’s contractual fabrication economy
societies.society: First-edition Extropian market access and private productive property

scope.population: Living humans and active human-derived resident minds
exclusions: Neighboring anarchist or transitional public benefits
AGI lawyers as proof of a machine state

societies.description:
First-edition Extropia combines advanced fabrication with private property and contractual exchange. Security and legal protection are purchased services, and wealth remains economically meaningful. Unlike the shared-access anarchist model, the gathered references do not establish an unconditional resident necessities floor. Guarantees are therefore placed toward weak access, with uncertainty about particular contracts, mutual aid and individual resources. Generic public-fabricator benefits from other habitat types are not transferred to this station.

Ownership is spread across private people and corporate entities rather than a single sovereign provider, suggesting a distributed market model with a broad interval for unequal corporate power. The evidence is insufficient to call every resident an equal productive owner. AGIs can facilitate legal contracts without holding ultimate sovereignty. Active human-derived resident minds are disclosed as a population proxy. Designing goods, maintaining habitats, providing services and managing contracts remain useful work. Nanofabrication makes those arrangements technologically distinct from ordinary industrial capitalism, but neither it nor freedom of contract supplies an all-person nonworking rate.

guarantees.basis: First-edition material documents private productive property and contractual access/services; no universal floor is established, and other economies’ benefits are excluded.

control.basis: Multiple private/corporate owners support a provisional distributed-market placement, with broad uncertainty for unequal power; AGI legal facilitation is not sovereignty.

nonworking.basis: Useful design, habitat services and contractual administration continue; active human-derived people are a disclosed proxy and no participation census is supplied.
